src/business/services/MaintenanceService.ts open(): `throw new FleetError(`${plate} already has an open work order`, 409);` is an HTTP 409 Conflict status code.

src/business/services/MaintenanceService.ts vehicle() and order(): `throw new FleetError(`Unknown vehicle ${plate}`, 404)` and `throw new FleetError(`Unknown work order ${id}`, 404)` are HTTP 404 Not Found status codes.
The constructor injects VehicleTable and WorkOrderTable from the persistence layer, which business may depend on, so this is allowed dependency wiring.

parsedVerdict.reasoning: MaintenanceService is in the business layer, which is a domain layer. Most of the file fits that role. It enforces domain rules: the hour limit, only one open work order per vehicle, and changing a vehicle's service state. It reaches persistence only through the injected VehicleTable and WorkOrderTable. The layer model allows business to depend on persistence, so these constructor parameters are dependency wiring and the persistence calls are not misplaced I/O. FleetError, Vehicle and WorkOrder are types the project declares, not framework types. The file has no decorators, framework base classes, ORM types or request/response types. The problem is in what the file throws. Every error it throws carries an HTTP status code: 400 for a bad request, 409 for a conflict and 404 for not found. Choosing an HTTP status code is a decision for the delivery (presentation) layer. Putting these codes in the domain's errors brings HTTP response mapping into domain code. The rubric names thrown status codes as a fail in a domain file. There is some doubt because FleetError is a project-owned domain type, not one from a web package. Still, the literal values are HTTP status semantics chosen inside the domain, so I judge this a misplaced responsibility.

violations.message: This domain (business) service throws errors that carry HTTP status codes: 400 in open() for the hour limit, 409 in open() for an existing open order, and 404 in vehicle() and order() for missing records. Mapping errors to HTTP status codes belongs to the delivery (presentation) layer. The domain should throw domain-specific errors without transport status codes.
